title: Algorithm Needs To Be Updated
body: The buying players and different game modes are good but the actual simulation of the games is just awful. I played over 10 games and lost more than half of them with having the better team. The game stresses fitness and focus and even with perfect fitness and focus you can still lose games to worse teams who are less fit and less focus. It’s so statistically impossible the game can’t justify it and it needs to update the algorithm of how games are simulated. If this is fixed then the game would be great and get a five star rating. Update: the response below is misleading the algorithm is still broken my squad with better training and better fitness and in a majority of cases a better team still loses. The developer will then claim tactics but I have stats to back up that my teams plays better and still loses so that’s not true. I dropped the rating down a star based on the developers response. It’s a simple fix: fix the algorithm where the team that is better trained, better fit and is better overall should generally win not be fighting really hard to get to .500. Do better

title: I would not recommend spending money and support sucks
body: I enjoyed the game, but I strongly recommend not spending real money on players or progression unless you fully understand the yearly Season Reset. I made purchases shortly after starting the game, only to learn that players and in-game progress from UFM26 reset and do not carry over into the new season. Support explained that previous squad performance can influence your new starting team, but you do not retain the actual players and progress you spent money building. For players spending real money, I believe this should be made extremely clear before every purchase, especially when a reset is approaching. The game can be fun, but buyers should know exactly what they’re paying for: your purchases may contribute to progress that will later be reset. I would recommend playing without spending money unless you’re comfortable with that system

title: Has potential
body: UFM 26 has some strong potential as a football manager game with updated rosters and a lot of strategic depth. However, there are some major drawbacks that make the experience frustrating. The biggest issue is the fitness recovery system—players regain stamina at just 1% per hour, which means it can take several days before they’re ready again unless you spend money. This ties into the second problem: heavy monetization pressures. The game is enjoyable for a handful of matches per day, but progress quickly stalls unless you buy energy packs or premium items. The training mechanics also feel tedious. Performance drops every night, so you’re constantly grinding to recover stats that just fall again the next day. On top of that, trade challenges are unnecessarily difficult without spending money, and the gameplay loop starts to feel more like a chore than a fun management experience. Visually, the game could use some upgrades. The match animations are repetitive, and not all real-world players are even available at launch, which is disappointing for fans who expect a full database. It also would be nice if the transfer market was easier to use and trade players with the system seems wonky on who you can sell because of them being on your starting 11 which doesn’t make sense. Overall, UFM 26 is a game with good ideas and potential, but the slow recovery times, paywalls, and repetitive design hold it back. Unless the developers rebalance the fitness and monetization systems, it’s hard to recommend beyond casual play.
